surfaces.part: seamless earth ground field with clods, grit and a few dry grass tufts

answer.evidence: This is a full-bleed terrain tile, not a standing object. The silhouette is 192 px wide on every row from 0 to 143, so it has no outline, no cap and no front face. The column scans show one continuous brown (#7b5d48, L~100) with only isolated 1-row darker specks (#654c39, L=81) at scattered rows. These are clod and grit marks, not edge lines or eave bands. There is no ellipse, roof or open container, so no object top surface or front face applies. The image reads as a flat, seamless ground texture, which is what the terrain kind expects.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a mostly flat brown field. Measured near-flat coverage is 56% against 0% for both references, so large areas have no dot, grain or variation. Only 3 visible tones per tile and 9 distinct colours in total, against 80 for the grass reference and 7 visible tones for the paving reference. The sparse speckles and the three small yellow tufts are tiny and widely spaced, so they do not give the clumped clods or grit clusters the brief describes. The raised clods barely read, and the soil shows no stepped highlight, mid, dark and deep ramp like Beodeul's. There is no outline, which is fine for a ground tile, but the shading is shallow and the surface looks like a flat fill with noise. A careful artist would not accept it next to the grass reference, which carries clumped grass texture in every tile.
